channel.title: Shulhan Arukh Orah Hayim — Dayan Daniel Kada
channel.description: Dayan Daniel Kada's Thursday-night class at Tiferet Eyal through the Shulhan Arukh, Orah Hayim, 2022-23: Shavuot, the Torah reading (Simanim 134-149), the shofar and Yom Kippur night.
channel.itunes:author: Dayan Daniel Kada

item.title: Must You Wait for Nightfall on Shavuot Night? | Shulhan Arukh Orah Hayim | Siman 494
item.description:
Does Shavuot night begin only at nightfall? Siman 494 covers the day's prayers and readings, then the Mishnah Berurah's custom of delaying Arbit so that the seven weeks are complete. The Rabbi traces its origin in Rabbi Avraham Horowitz, the Magen Avraham and the Taz, and calls it difficult.

item.title: Why Start Shavuot with Dairy, Then Meat? | Shulhan Arukh Orah Hayim | Siman 494
item.description:
Why eat dairy first and then meat on Shavuot? The shiur also covers berakhot after a night of learning, including that a berakhah on food covers the whole night, which morning berakhot are said after a real sleep, and the difference between dozing and a fixed sleep.

item.title: Why Do We Lift the Torah Before Reading It? | Shulhan Arukh Orah Hayim | Simanim 134-135
item.description:

item.title: What If the Kohen Is in the Middle of Shema? | Shulhan Arukh Orah Hayim | Siman 135
item.description:
If the only Kohen present is in the middle of Shema or the Amidah when the Torah is taken out, he is not called. The class goes through Shulhan Arukh siman 135, the Mishnah Berurah's additions, and a table of when a Kohen is called and whether he goes up if called anyway.

item.title: Can Two People Read the Torah at Once? | Shulhan Arukh Orah Hayim | Simanim 140-141
item.description:
What if a reader loses his voice, or two people begin reading together? Siman 140 to 141 covers interruptions in the Torah reading. If the first reader had finished three verses he says the closing berakhah, and otherwise the next reader starts from the beginning with berakhot before and after.

item.title: May You Touch the Sefer Torah With Bare Hands? | Shulhan Arukh Orah Hayim | Siman 147
item.description:
